QA audit by qa-b2df68b9, 2026-08-09 ~15:06Z. Full evidence for the rejection. **The split itself is correct and I verified it independently — do not touch the code. The fix is evidence-only.**

## Verified PASSING (re-measured by me, not read from the report)

**DoD 1 — per-file cap.** `grep -c ''` (exact; PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` skips blank lines and `wc -l` drops one without a trailing newline):
```
187  packages/scheduler/src/graph-internal.ts
245  packages/scheduler/src/graph-traversal.ts
249  packages/scheduler/src/frontier.ts
248  packages/scheduler/src/frontier-cursor.ts
```
All <=250, none >=400. `graph-model.ts` (337) and `validate-graph-input.ts` (331) are over 250 but pre-existing and NOT in commit `503d127` — they are not "resulting files" and are correctly out of scope.

**DoD 2 — public root surface unchanged.** `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts` is byte-identical across the split (not in the commit at all). The five names that left `graph-internal.ts`'s direct-export set — `compareStrings`, `findCycleCore`, `topologicalOrder`, `CycleCore`, `TopoResult` — are re-exported at `graph-internal.ts:14-15` from `./graph-traversal.js`, so the module surface is preserved by re-export rather than relocated. `frontier.ts`'s direct-export name set is identical to its parent. `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` exit 0.

**Zero test edits** — stronger than DoD 3's "no test edits beyond import paths". `git show --name-only 503d127` contains no `.test.` path.

**Commit hygiene.** `503d127` is exactly the 6 owned paths, 520 insertions / 416 deletions, no foreign path rode along.

## The defect — DoD 3, "scheduler suites green"

The recorded `verification.command` was:
```
pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler exec vitest run --root ../.. \
  packages/scheduler/src --exclude '**/package-boundary.test.ts'
```
`packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` is an **owned path** and it is **red**. Run unexcluded by me:
```
Test Files  1 failed | 35 passed (36)
     Tests  1 failed | 674 passed (675)
```
The recorded `outputTail` says `Test Files 35 passed (35) / Tests 635 passed (635) / GATE_EXIT=0`. Anyone auditing this task by its outputTail concludes the package is fully green. It is not, and that number becomes a false baseline for the next task that diffs against it.

Epic rail 3 permits completing with foreign red — but it requires the merge-base failing set, the HEAD failing set, the delta intersected with owned paths, and **the foreign red reported verbatim**. This task has **zero comments**: no baseline, no verbatim red, no attribution. The architect's own handoff pitfall said "attribute existing daemon-main package-boundary red" — attribute, not exclude.

## Attribution I already did for you — do not re-derive it

The red is genuinely foreign and pre-existing:
```
FAIL packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts
  > keeps scheduler registrars behind the package-root import boundary
Error: boundary scan failed for apps\daemon\src\daemon-main.ts:
  Error: unterminated regular expression source token
  at packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts:300:15
```
`apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts` is **byte-identical at `503d127^` and HEAD** (`cmp` clean), last touched by `749eb46` (task-f01ef545, Linux platform observation boundary), and is not in your commit. `package-boundary.test.ts` was not modified either. Same test code + same input bytes = same failure at merge-base. So delta ∩ owned-paths = EMPTY and the task is completable — the evidence just has to say so.

Also foreign, and newer than your run: `pnpm typecheck` repo-wide is now exit 1 on `packages/runner` — `src/scope/scope-git.test.ts` TS2305/TS2339/TS7006. That file is **untracked** (`??`), another agent's in-flight TDD red. Your `typecheck=0 (all 12 projects Done)` was true at 15:02:36; this landed after. Not yours, and not something to chase.

## Separate finding — not yours to fix, flagging so it is not lost

`package-boundary.test.ts:288` iterates roots `["adapters", "apps", "packages"]` in that order and the `catch` at :299 **throws**, aborting the whole scan. Because `apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts` throws, the entire `packages/` half of the boundary scan has never executed for as long as that file has been unparseable. So this test's red is not merely noisy — its eventual *green* will also be meaningless until either the scan collects failures instead of throwing, or daemon-main.ts parses. Root cause is a foreign file, so this needs its own task; do not widen scope to fix it here.
